title: An XLSB cell-value commit parses the workbook once, not twice, and a proven no-op parses it not at all
code_state: crates/litchi-xlsb/src/cell_values/workbook.rs and crates/litchi-xlsb/src/workbook/package.rs changed; tests added in crates/litchi-xlsb/src/workbook/tests.rs and crates/litchi-xlsb/tests/cell_value_edit.rs; tools/perf-baseline gains one fixture-generator binary
implements: item XLSB-1 (rank 19) of change 0587, in full
reason_codes: an exact no-op cell-value commit cloned the package and reparsed the whole workbook from bytes the callee had just proved byte-identical; both are now skipped and the workbook is kept

a real edit took three OpcPackage clones, one worksheet-blob copy and two independent full Workbook parses of the same candidate bytes, discarding the first parse after validating against it; the validated parse is now what gets published, so one parse and two clones are gone

value identity is by construction: from_opc_package_with_external_link_limits is a pure function of the package and the external-link limits, and both branches feed it the same bytes it was fed before
atomicity is strictly tighter than before, because nothing the caller owns is touched until every check has passed and the single assignment is the last statement
the public apply and apply_with_external_link_limits keep their signatures, their &mut OpcPackage publication contract and their error identity

accepted_evidence.instruction_counts: callgrind isolation pairs at 5 and 15 samples, differenced over 10, pinned to CPU 17: testVarious.xlsb no-op 52,308,801 -> 29,325,884 Ir/op (-43.94%), one-cell edit 78,314,813 -> 54,162,314 (-30.84%); synthetic-4x2000x12.xlsb no-op 188,809,497 -> 175,541,374 (-7.03%), edit 357,557,295 -> 343,509,287 (-3.93%)
accepted_evidence.mechanism_attribution: the per-symbol difference on testVarious.xlsb is identical to the instruction between the no-op case and the edit case (mce::codec::BoundedOutput::extend_from_slice -71,907,399 in both over ten extra samples, and likewise for realloc, RawVecInner::finish_grow, quick_xml attributes and mce::codec::esc), which is the signature of exactly one Workbook parse removed in each; the 1,169,582 Ir by which the two cases differ is the edit path's two extra Arc-sharing package clones and its worksheet-blob copy
accepted_evidence.paired_timing: order A1 B1 B2 A2 plus an A3/A4 A-A control pair in the same window, 40 samples per leg after 3 warmups, all 8 xlsb_crud cases on 4 fixtures; testVarious.xlsb p50 no-op -46.43%, one edit -31.40%, ceil(1%) edits -29.38%; cond_format.xlsb -9.69%, -9.69%, -8.29%; every commit case moved down on every fixture and the largest positive p50 delta in the 32 case-by-fixture cells is +1.93%, on an untouched read path, against a 5% review trigger
accepted_evidence.in_run_control: the five read-only cases never reach apply_cell_values and moved -3.54% to +1.93%, bounding drift and code layout; subtracting that offset from the no-op delta gives about -43% against the deterministic -43.94% of instructions
accepted_evidence.differential: 17 artifact paths (all 15 .xlsb fixtures under test-data/, two of which are byte-identical copies, plus two synthetic), 35 worksheets: catalogs, per-worksheet snapshot and cell digests, an exact no-op commit and a real scalar edit per worksheet with published digests, saved-package digests and readbacks, and one refused publication per artifact with its typed error and a byte-identity check; the two legs' reports are byte-identical
accepted_evidence.harness_gates: 192 observations across 6 legs x 4 fixtures x 8 cases: every applicable xlsb_crud gate true, changed package members empty for every no-op case and exactly one worksheet part for every edit case, output SHA-256 identical across all six legs
accepted_evidence.tests: three in-crate tests over an exhaustively destructured whole-Workbook projection (no-op publishes nothing and stays a parse of its own package; a real edit installs a workbook equal to a fresh parse of the published bytes; a refusal leaves the projection unchanged) and two public-boundary byte-identity tests

accepted_costs.aa_floor: this window's A-A floor is worse than the host's standing figure: over 64 control pairs, |p50 delta| median 0.84%, p90 3.22%, max 10.04%; |p99 delta| median 1.75%, p90 10.57%, max 31.59%
accepted_costs.not_separable: on synthetic-4x500x8.xlsb (-7.90%, -4.76%, -4.98%) and synthetic-4x2000x12.xlsb (-1.60%, -2.49%, -2.36%) the commit deltas are inside that fixture's own A-A range or the same size as its untouched read-only drift; nothing is claimed from their timing
accepted_costs.instruction_counts: instructions rank work, not latency; callgrind counts rep movsb per byte and runs SHA-256 in software, and the per-op figure includes the harness's own out-of-band output hashing, which is constant across legs
accepted_costs.corpus: the saving tracks a workbook's feature surface rather than its size; on the feature-rich 22.7 KB real producer it is 44% of a no-op commit and save, on a feature-free 324 KB synthetic 7%. No large real-producer .xlsb exists in this corpus, so the figure for one is unknown and bounded by those two

known_gaps.unmeasured_resources: bytes read, syscalls, peak RSS and allocation counts; allocations are removed by construction (a whole parse and one package clone on the no-op path; a parse, two package clones and one worksheet-blob copy on the edit path) but none was counted, and xlsb_crud has no allocator-metrics hookup
known_gaps.sibling_sites: cell_values::root::insert_candidate_cell (root.rs:233) and transfer_cell (root.rs:1253) still reparse the package a second time into *workbook after calling apply_with_external_link_limits; each would lose one further parse by taking Applied::Published directly. They are reached only through apply_workbook_structure, for which no harness selector exists, so they were left unmeasured rather than changed unmeasured
known_gaps.unanswered_question: Workbook::apply_sparklines and Workbook::apply_cell_watches publish straight into &mut self.package and never refresh the derived workbook fields; whether that is intended is a correctness question this record does not answer
known_gaps.synthetic_fixtures: producer-free: no pivot cache, structured table, chart sheet, drawing, connection, external link or VBA project. They answer whether the commit path scales with cell count and nothing about real-producer feature surface

withheld: any speedup, regression, cold-cache, physical-device, range-source, peak-RSS, allocation-profile, concurrency-scaling or cross-platform result
any timing statement about the two synthetic fixtures, whose deltas fall inside this window's A-A floor
